item.title: Movement-specific effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation over premotor and parietal cortices after stroke
item.description:
[预印本] medRxiv
Background: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) has been proposed to support post-stroke motor recovery, but the response may depend on the task and motor-network status. We aimed to compare how premotor and parietal stimulation affects performance across reach directions with different movement demands, in preparation for therapeutic application of TMS. Methods: 16 participants with chronic subcortical stroke performed planar reaches with the KINARM exoskeleton toward distal and proximal targets. Before movement, a 10-Hz triple-pulse TMS train was delivered over bilateral dorsal or ventral premotor cortex (PMd, PMv) or dorsomedial posterior parietal cortex (PPC) at subthreshold and suprathreshold intensities. The parietal midline was used as the control target. Participant-level bootstrap confidence intervals assessed changes in trajectory straightness and smoothness relative to the control target and differences between reach directions. We compared motor-network activity and connectivity using task-based and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from participants with stroke and neurologically intact controls. To explore response variability, we tested associations between TMS response and motor impairment, resting-state connectivity, and the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement. Results: Suprathreshold PMd and PPC stimulation in both hemispheres improved trajectory straightness or smoothness during distal reaches relative to the control target. Suprathreshold contralesional PMd stimulation increased trajectory deviation and reduced smoothness during proximal reaches. Baseline performance during distal reaches was more closely related to motor impairment, and contralesional PMd effects were more favorable during distal than proximal reaches across all kinematic measures. Participants with stroke showed lower bilateral PMv activation during movement and stronger interhemispheric PPC connectivity. Only the change in task-evoked activity at the stimulated region from planning to movement was related to TMS response. Smaller changes relative to controls were associated with more favorable kinematic effects during distal reaches. Conclusions: Movements more affected after stroke were the most responsive to this type of stimulation. The response to TMS was also associated with task-evoked activity differences at the stimulated region between movement planning and execution. Neuromodulation may therefore be most effective when designed around both the pathophysiology of the cortical target and the type of movement.

item.title: Acute scalp EEG signatures of anterior thalamic DBS in epilepsy:reproducible gamma power enhancement within an aperiodic spectral-state shift
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv
Background: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the anterior nucleus of the thalamus (ANT) is an established treatment for drug-resistant epilepsy, but acute scalp-EEG signatures of stimulation remain incompletely characterized. Objective: To identify acute scalp-EEG signatures of ANT-DBS and assess their cross-year reproducibility in a proof-of-concept repeated-session cohort. Methods: Scalp EEG from five patients recorded one year apart (10 sessions) was analyzed during nominal cyclic DBS (1 s ON, ~5 s OFF). DBS ON was compared with the within-cycle OFFmean and consecutive post-offset OFF windows using power spectral density (PSD), spatiotemporal-frequency (STF) analysis, and spectral parameterization. Results: DBS ON showed higher 30-70 Hz gamma power than OFFmean in all sessions (median +0.94 dB), with significant PSD clusters overlapping gamma in 10/10 sessions. STF identified gamma increases as the most reproducible spatiotemporal effect. Exploratory frontal 34-44 Hz and central 56-70 Hz components showed cross-year support, and the broader pattern persisted when 48-52 or 45-55 Hz were excluded before clustering. Lower-frequency effects were more heterogeneous and weakened from early to late OFF windows. Aperiodic parameterization showed lower ON exponent and offset in all sessions (Delta chi = -0.20; Delta b = -0.25). After correction, theta suppression was not preserved, whereas a smaller low-gamma residual remained. Conclusions: ANT-DBS was associated with consistent acute scalp-EEG state signatures comprising raw gamma enhancement, lower aperiodic exponent and offset, and a modest residual low-gamma effect. These hypothesis-generating findings show that scalp EEG can capture acute ANT-DBS state changes, while larger prospective studies are needed to establish clinical relevance.

item.title: Preoperative diffusion-perivascular MRI burden and postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation in Parkinson disease
item.description:
[预印本] Research Square
Abstract Postoperative delirium after subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation may reflect pre-existing brain vulnerability, but the preoperative imaging correlates of this vulnerability remain uncertain. We examined whether a combined diffusion and perivascular imaging burden was associated with delirium after bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation. This single-centre observational cohort included 100 patients with Parkinson disease undergoing bilateral subthalamic nucleus deep brain stimulation and 32 healthy controls scanned with the same preoperative MRI protocol. Delirium was assessed during postoperative days using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale with clinical adjudication. Age- and sex-adjusted reference models fitted in healthy controls were used to standardise tract diffusion metrics, diffusion tensor image analysis along the perivascular space, and basal ganglia enlarged perivascular space counts. Directionally aligned diffusion and perivascular scores were averaged with equal domain weights. Patients who developed postoperative delirium (n = 30) had higher combined burden than those who did not (n = 70; 95% CI, 0.584 to 1.526; q<.001). Using Firth penalised logistic regression, higher combined burden remained associated with postoperative delirium after adjustment for age, sex, education, Mini-Mental State Examination score, disease duration, and motor severity (95% CI, 1.49 to 4.25; Wald P<.001). Higher burden was also associated with longer delirium duration and higher peak screening scores among affected patients. Exploratory internal prediction yielded an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.701 after adding burden to clinical variables, compared with 0.538 for clinical variables alone. These findings support preoperative diffusion-perivascular burden as a candidate marker of perioperative neuropsychiatric vulnerability requiring multicentre validation.

item.title: A Dual-Stream Spatio-Temporal Network with Bidirectional Rectification for Differential Diagnosis of Dementia using EEG
item.description:
[预印本] Research Square
Abstract Accurate differential diagnosis between Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) is of critical importance for the early screening of neurodegenerative diseases. Scalp electroencephalogram (EEG), as a non-invasive neurophysiological detection tool with excellent temporal resolution, has been widely adopted in dementia screening research. However, the inherent low signal-to-noise ratio and non-stationarity of scalp EEG signals, combined with the highly overlapping pathological rhythms between AD and FTD patients, render existing single-domain representation methods incapable of achieving precise pathological differentiation. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dual-stream spatio-temporal network. In this framework, multiscale temporal features and effective connectivity graph features are extracted in parallel, followed by their integration. However, directly fusing the features from the two streams tends to amplify their respective noises. Therefore, the Spatio-Temporal Feature Fusion Based on Bidirectional Rectification module is proposed to execute dynamic noise suppression on the features and subsequently performs deep feature fusion via a cross-attention mechanism. Furthermore, this paper applies knowledge distillation using attention maps to address the issue of imbalanced sample distributions in the dataset. Experimental results on the ADFTD-RS dataset show that the proposed framework yields a subject-level accuracy of 60.00\% and an F1-score of 57.44\%, showing measurable improvements over several baseline methods. This work offers a feasible approach for the computer-aided differential diagnosis of dementia based on resting-state EEG.

item.title: Sensorimotor cortex activity during cued gait differs in Parkinson's freezers and non-freezers
item.description:
[预印本] medRxiv
Gait impairments are a major contributor to disability in patients with Parkinson's disease despite dopaminergic and neuromodulation therapies. External cues (e.g., visual targets, rhythmic auditory sounds) are commonly used to improve gait quality and reduce freezing of gait (FOG), yet their effectiveness varies across patients and contexts. Improved understanding of the neural mechanisms of cueing benefits is essential to personalize rehabilitation strategies and improve outcomes. We use mobile electroencephalography (EEG) to test the hypothesis that cues improve gait through engagement of voluntary motor control mechanisms to compensate for impaired gait automaticity. In addition, we investigate whether this mechanism is related to cueing benefits or freezing status. Eighteen PD patients with a history of freezing (PD-F), 21 patients without freezing (PD-NF) and 19 age-matched healthy controls (HC) walked overground under three conditions: normal walking, synchronizing to auditory cues, and stepping over visual cues. Stride-locked beta band (13-30 Hz) power dynamics in sensorimotor cortex were used to measure cortical control of stepping. Spatiotemporal gait parameters improved with cues in all groups. However, PD-F had smaller cue-related gains in speed and stride length when compared with PD-NF for both cue types, and did not improve gait speed with visual cues. EEG revealed greater contralateral sensorimotor cortex swing-phase beta suppression in PD-F than PD-NF patients, with visual cues eliciting the most robust response. In contrast, beta suppression with cues was less pronounced in PD-NF and HC, despite greater behavioral gains. In addition, engagement of sensorimotor cortex during visual cueing was associated with divergent gait effects across PD subgroups: In PD-NF greater beta suppression was associated with less gait improvement, whereas in PD-F the opposite was observed. These findings suggest distinct sensorimotor control mechanisms for cue utilization in PD-F and PD-NF, and indicate that engagement of voluntary motor control circuits may underlie cueing benefits primarily in PD-F.

item.title: REM Sleep Iota Oscillations Across the Lifespan
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv
Iota oscillations are a newly discovered marker of wakefulness and rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. So far, iota in REM sleep has only been reported in the surface electroencephalography (EEG) of a small sample of young adults and in intracranial recordings of epileptic patients. Here, we investigated the presence of these oscillations in a large dataset (N=937) of high-density sleep EEG recordings from individuals 7 to 70 years old. We found that iota spectral peaks during REM sleep were between 25 and 40 Hz, slightly faster than in wake (25-35 Hz). Iota power was significantly associated with REM sleep architecture, increasing with both REM duration and across progressive sleep cycles. Iota peaks were observed in individuals of all ages, although the prevalence decreased gradually with age, from 88% in children to 44% in older adults. Most iota spectral peak properties (frequency, amplitude, timing, topography) likewise shifted with age. The most striking effect, however, was in bandwidth, such that children had narrow iota peaks, older adults had broad iota peaks, and 20-30 year olds could have either. It remains unclear whether narrowband and broadband iota are functionally equivalent. On shorter time scales (< 1 year), iota properties remained stable across measurements. Analyses of a separate dataset of monozygotic and dizygotic twins revealed high heritability of all iota peak properties except bandwidth. Overall, these results establish iota as a genetically determined trait-like marker of REM sleep with unique age-related changes. Iota oscillations open new avenues to investigate the interaction between sleep, genetics, development, and aging.

item.title: Comparing re-referencing methods for human intracranial EEG
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv
Stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) involves the implantation of depth electrodes in the brain to monitor epileptic seizures for surgical feasibility. As the electrodes advance into deeper limbic structures, the macro contacts distributed along the shaft record electrical activity from more lateral sites, while a bundled array of microwires simultaneously captures highly localised signals from the tip of the electrode. In a clinical setting these electrical signals are recorded relative to a reference signal, which may be sub-optimal for subsequent analyses that are unrelated to clinical objectives. Therefore, a secondary re-referencing operation is often undertaken to transform the signal in relation to a specific hypothesis. Despite a recent surge in SEEG studies, comparative studies on the much-understudied issue of re-referencing are sparse. Here, we analyse data collected from 16 human patients during an episodic memory task and comparatively apply a range of re-referencing methods to both macro contact and micro-wire data. We find that the choice of method changes the proportion of trials that survive artefact rejection, low frequency power, and the aperiodic background against which that power is read. In the hippocampal recordings, however, no method differed from any other in the size of a memory effect in power or spike-field coherence. This early transformative decision therefore bears on how the signal is described. We found no evidence that it changes the detectability of the behavioural effects tested here, and no method reversed the direction of a memory effect.

item.title: Neurodegeneration epicenters: Distinct network mechanisms of dopaminergic treatment in Parkinson's disease.
item.description:
Neural regeneration research
Abstract Parkinson's disease exhibits heterogeneous spatiotemporal patterns of neurodegeneration. Dopaminergic therapy improves motor symptoms by modulating brain function in affected regions, yet whether the neural mechanisms through which dopaminergic therapy exerts its effects are linked to this heterogeneity of neurodegeneration remains unclear. A connectivity-based epicenter framework combined with spectral dynamic causal modeling was applied to resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data from 160 drug-naïve Parkinson's disease patients and 174 healthy controls to identify subtype-specific degenerative epicenters and characterize directional interactions among affected regions. Ninety-seven patients additionally underwent an acute levodopa challenge to evaluate how dopaminergic modulation influences these interactions and relates to symptom improvements. Two distinct Parkinson's disease subtypes were identified: subtype 1 was characterized by degenerative epicenters predominantly located in subcortical and cerebellar regions, whereas subtype 2 exhibited epicenters primarily involving cortical regions. Both subtypes exhibited widespread dysregulation of directional interactions among epicenter regions relative to healthy controls. Levodopa treatment partially reversed these network abnormalities in a manner specific to each subtype, notably within cerebellar vermis in subtype 1 and frontal cortex in subtype 2. Symptom improvements were linked to distinct network interactions: in subtype 1, tremor correlated with the thalamus, midbrain nuclei, and cerebellar vermis, whereas bradykinesia primarily involved the cerebellar vermis; in subtype 2, rigidity improvements mapped to frontal cortex and limbic regions, and bradykinesia to limbic regions. These findings suggest that Parkinson's disease involves distinct epicenter networks in each subtype, with widespread directional dysregulation contributing to symptom diversity in patients. Levodopa treatment selectively modulates these network interactions, shedding light on the mechanisms underlying treatment heterogeneity and guiding precision-targeted therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Predictive EEG Signatures of Alzheimer's Disease: A Cross-Validated, Cross-Method Analysis Using ANCOVA Filtering and Sparse Logistic Regression
item.description:
[预印本] Research Square
Abstract Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) changes how the brain’s electrical activity behaves, and these changes can, in principle, be picked up directly from a resting-state EEG recording without any invasive testing. This study asks a much narrower question: does a small subset of four EEG-derived measurement families, namely signal complexity, spectral power, functional connectivity and network topology, reliably separate individuals with AD from Healthy Controls (HC), and does that separation hold up under strict, leakage-free testing? Using a public dataset of 36 AD and 29 HC subjects, candidate features were selected through permutation-based ANCOVA with false discovery rate correction, controlling for age and gender, and each selected feature was then re-checked using a complementary method (Mann-Whitney U with FDR correction, plus network-based statistics for connectivity), applied to the same subjects, to confirm the finding wasn’t an artifact of the first method’s particular assumptions. Agreement between the two methods was strong for signal complexity (Jaccard = 0.85) and spectral power (Jaccard = 0.87), essentially perfect for two of the four network measures (Jaccard = 1.00), and weaker for connectivity (Jaccard = 0.60, assessed at the level of frequency bands). A sparse logistic regression classifier was then trained using 5-fold cross-validation in which feature selection was independently repeated inside each fold, a design specifically intended to stop information from test subjects leaking into which features get chosen. This classifier reached 78.5% ± 5.8% accuracy at discriminating AD from HC (sensitivity 0.803 ± 0.116, specificity 0.753 ± 0.100, AUC 0.808 ± 0.134). A single spectral power feature was among the two features retained in three of the five folds, more than any other individual feature. Taken together, the results point to a real but modest EEG signature of AD in this dataset, identified using a validation design built specifically so that reported accuracy reflects genuine generalization rather than an artifact of how the features were selected.

item.title: Molecularly distinct neurodegeneration shapes the DOPA-dependent dynamic of large-scale brain connectomics in GBA-associated Parkinson’s disease
item.description:
[预印本] Research Square
Abstract GBA1-associated Parkinson’s disease (GBA1-PD) is a biologically distinct synucleinopathy associated with glucocerebrosidase deficiency, lysosomal dysfunction, and more extensive cortical neurodegeneration. How these molecular abnormalities shape large-scale cortical network dynamics in vivo remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize resting-state EEG functional connectivity and network topology in GBA1-PD and to determine whether GBA1-related molecular pathology is associated with a distinct oscillatory connectome signature and its modulation by dopaminergic treatment. We recorded resting-state EEG in 22 patients with PD (GBA1-PD = 7; LRRK2-PD = 5; sporadic PD = 10) together with 14 age-matched healthy controls. EEG was acquired in OFF and ON dopaminergic states. Functional connectivity was estimated using imaginary coherence (ImCoh) and phase-locking value (PLV) across canonical frequency bands, while network organization was quantified using the graph-theoretical clustering coefficient. Linear mixed-effects models were used to assess therapy- and subtype-specific effects. GBA1-PD exhibited a selective increase in gamma-band clustering coefficient in the ON condition (p = 0.044), which was not observed in LRRK2 or sporadic PD. PLV-based analyses highlighted opposite clustering changes in GBA1 and LRRK2 patients. ImCoh analyses further revealed different therapy-related connectivity changes in genetic and sporadic PD across all frequency bands (all p ≤ 0.0035). Compared with healthy controls, PD was associated with widespread disruption of cortico-cortical connectivity. All significant effects were abolished in surrogate-data analyses, supporting their physiological specificity. Resting-state EEG connectomics may reveal genotype-specific network alterations in GBA1-PD and their modulation by dopaminergic treatment, supporting a relationship between genetic background and large-scale brain network dynamics.

item.title: ADHDeepNet: An Explainable Framework for EEG-Based ADHD Detection From Raw Signals.
item.description:
Biomedical physics & engineering express
Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a common brain disorder in children that can persist into adulthood, affecting social, academic, and career life. Early diagnosis is crucial for managing these impacts on patients and the healthcare system but is often labor-intensive and time-consuming. This paper presents a novel method to improve ADHD diagnosis precision and timeliness by leveraging Deep Learning (DL) approaches and electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. We introduce ADHDeepNet, a deep learning model that utilizes comprehensive temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability techniques optimized for EEG signals. ADHDeepNet integrates feature extraction and refinement processes to enhance ADHD diagnosis. The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 Healthy Controls), employing nested cross-validation for robust performance. The proposed two-stage methodology uses a 10-fold cross-subject validation strategy. Initially, each iteration optimizes the model's hyper-parameters with inner 2-fold cross-validation. Then, Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN) with various standard deviations and magnification levels is applied for data augmentation. ADHDeepNet achieved 100% sensitivity and 99.17% accuracy in classifying ADHD/HC subjects. To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers. Additionally, t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) visualized high-dimensional data, aiding in interpreting the model's decisions. This study highlights the potential of deep learning and EEG in enhancing ADHD diagnosis accuracy and efficiency.

item.title: The spatial extent of fast ripples is associated with cognitive and language deficits in children with focal epilepsy: An exploratory SEEG study.
item.description:
Epilepsy & behavior : E&B
Objective To determine if the spatial extent of interictal fast ripples in focal epilepsy patients is associated with brain dysfunction. Methods Thirty pediatric focal epilepsy patients who underwent SEEG investigation had their cognitive and language deficits assessed in scales of 0 to 4. Fast ripples (250-500 Hz), ripples (80-250 Hz), and IEDs were automatically detected in 10 min during NREM sleep. We fitted linear models to the relationship between the cognitive deficit scale and the spatial spread of the interictal neurophysiologic events (number of channels with rate of events > 10 % of maximum rate). For the language deficit, we computed the Spearman correlation between the median rate of events in all brain regions and the deficit scale. Results Cognitive deficit scale was significantly associated with the number of channels with fast ripples (p = 0.049), not so with ripples (p = 0.31), IEDs (p = 0.31). The potential confound of number of explored channels did not improve the fitting of the models. Language deficits were not correlated with the number of channels showing interictal events. However, from all brain regions the most statistically significant correlations (p < 0.01) were between median fast ripple rates in the left and right pars opercularis and triangularis of the inferior frontal gyrus (Broca's area and its contralateral counterpart) with r = 0.66, p = 0.003 (18 patients), in the superior temporal gyrus in the language dominant hemisphere with r = 0.72, p = 0.005 (13 patients), and the dominant basal temporal region with r = 0.79, p = 0.006 (10 patients). Median rates of IEDs and ripples exhibited lower correlation with language deficits in these regions. Conclusion Widespread fast ripples are associated with increased cognitive deficits, and language deficiencies are correlated with fast ripple rates in brain regions associated with language. The extent of fast-ripple activity was associated with cognitive deficit severity in this cohort, whereas the corresponding associations for ripples and IEDs did not reach statistical significance.

item.title: Generalized Spike-Wave discharges and myoclonic features in a subgroup of children with Self-Limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes.
item.description:
Epilepsy & behavior : E&B
Objective Generalized spike-wave discharges (GSWD) are occasionally observed in patients with self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS), but their clinical significance remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize the electroclinical features of these patients and to explore their potential clinical implications. Methods We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of 148 children diagnosed with SeLECTS at Xuanwu Hospital from June 2015 to October 2025. Patients with GSWD on electroencephalography were identified and compared with those without GSWD regarding demographic characteristics, seizure semiology, auxiliary examination findings, treatment response, and outcomes. Results GSWD were identified in 9 of 148 patients (6.1 %) with SeLECTS. These 9 patients included 4 males and 5 females, with a median onset age of 8 (IQR: 5-10) years. Compared with those without GSWD, they more frequently showed wakefulness seizures (44.4 % vs 5.8 %, p < 0.05), generalized tonic-clonic seizures during sleep (44.4 %), and myoclonic manifestations (77.8 %). Other clinical variables were similar between groups. All 9 patients achieved freedom from focal and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, though one required prolonged combination therapy. Two patients with follow-up exceeding 10 years showed electroclinical evolution toward juvenile myoclonic epilepsy, characterized by the absence of centrotemporal spikes, with generalized spike-wave bursts recurring on later EEGs. Conclusion We identified a subgroup of patients with SeLECTS characterized by the coexistence of GSWD and myoclonic features, showing partial electroclinical overlap with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy. These findings broaden the electroclinical spectrum of SeLECTS, though the relationship between focal and generalized network dysfunction in this subgroup requires confirmation in larger, prospectively followed cohorts.

item.title: Intrinsic and extrinsic connectivity of the seizure onset zone at rest and during stimulation.
item.description:
Brain stimulation
Background About half of patients who undergo epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy have seizure recurrence, supporting the need for approaches that more accurately identify the epileptogenic zone, defined as the brain areas whose removal causes cessation of seizures. Altered network connectivity has emerged as a candidate biomarker of the epileptogenic zone, but how connectivity is altered in the epileptogenic zone remains uncertain, with prior studies reporting inconsistent results. Hypothesis We hypothesized that a difference in intrinsic versus extrinsic connectivity of the epileptogenic zone may explain prior discrepant findings. Methods We retrospectively studied a multicenter cohort of 37 adult and 42 pediatric patients who underwent intracranial EEG recording and brain stimulation as part of epilepsy surgery planning. We measured spontaneous connectivity using Pearson correlation and perturbational connectivity using stimulation evoked potentials, modeling the connectivity according to the location of contacts in relation to the seizure onset zone while controlling for inter-electrode distance. Results For both adult and pediatric patients, resting connectivity was higher within compared to outside the seizure onset zone. However, resting connectivity between channels within and outside seizure onset zone was reduced. Stimulation connectivity followed a similar pattern, with elevated connectivity within the seizure onset zone but reduced connectivity from within to outside seizure onset zone. Significance These results support the hypothesis that the seizure onset zone is disconnected from the rest of the brain but intrinsically hyperconnected. This result helps reconcile prior inconsistencies across studies, aligns with basic science studies, and suggests an approach for future translational work aiming to localize the epileptogenic zone.

item.title: Along-tract statistical mapping of white matter abnormalities in children with SeLECTS.
item.description:
Brain research bulletin
Background and purpose Emerging evidence suggests that self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) may reflect atypical neurodevelopment. As WM maturation extends from the second trimester through adolescence, this study aimed to identify regions of delayed or aberrant white matter (WM) development in children with SeLECTS using along-tract statistical mapping for precise localization of microstructural alterations. Materials and methods 38 children with SeLECTS and 31 healthy controls underwent diffusion-weighted MRI scan. Fractional anisotropy (FA), mean diffusivity (MD), and radial diffusivity (RD) were derived from the diffusion tensor model. Whole-brain tractography was performed using deterministic EuDX tracking and registered to a standardized bundle atlas in MNI space. Thirty WM tracts per subject were extracted. Linear mixed models within the BUAN tractometry framework were used to assess segment wise group differences, while partial correlations were performed to evaluate associations between diffusion metrics and cognitive performance. FDR correction was applied per bundle for all comparisons. Results After FDR correction, children with SeLECTS showed increased MD in the forceps minor, midbody of the corpus callosum, right corticospinal tract, right extreme capsule, and bilateral uncinate fasciculi. MD values in the affected WM segments showed negative correlations with performance and full-scale IQ, and the segments showing significant correlations overlapped with those showing significant group differences. Conclusions SeLECTS is associated with MD-based microstructural alterations in superficial frontal, temporal, and parietal pathways, potentially indicating delayed white matter maturation.

item.title: Hidden Markov Modeling Reveals Altered Functional Network Dynamics in Multiple Sclerosis
item.description:
[预印本] bioRxiv
ABSTRACT Purpose Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a neurodegenerative and demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Recent evidence suggests that localized gray matter atrophy in MS may be involved in distributed functional brain networks. However, the dynamic trajectory of functional network alterations in MS remains unclear. The current study extends prior network-mediated findings and aims to investigate the dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) and energetic landscape across an atrophy-prone network in MS. Methods Twenty MS participants and twenty healthy controls (HC) underwent resting-state fMRI. The atrophy-based functional network (AFN) model was implemented, and time series from atrophy-prone regions were fit to a 12-state hidden Markov model. Each functional network state, a recurring pattern of activity across the AFN, was characterized by the AFN regions with the strongest activation. The states were then grouped into two metastates. Dynamic functional network metrics were compared between groups by permutation testing and correlated with disability and cognition. The energetic landscape of the network was mapped with a pairwise maximum-entropy model. Temporal irreversibility was also measured, which defines the arrow-of-time asymmetry of network dynamics. Results People with MS showed lower occupancy of state 1, which peaked on the right middle frontal and anterior cingulate cortex. Occupancy and mean lifetime were higher in states 3 and 10 (p < 0.05). In state 3, cortical activity was below the network average, and state 10 peaked on the postcentral gyrus. At the metastate level, MS participants spent more time in metastate M1 and less in M2 (p = 0.04). Within the MS group, a longer interval between visits to state 3 was associated with greater disability (r = 0.57), and a higher switching rate in state 10 with poorer verbal fluency (r = −0.50). The energetic landscape was similar between groups. Temporal irreversibility was lower in MS, mainly across subcortical connections. Conclusion MS participants dwelled longer in specific dFC states of the AFN, while the rate of transition between states did not differ from healthy controls. Dynamic functional network metrics were associated with disability and cognitive performance and may serve as functional correlates of clinical impairment. The states were similar between groups, whereas the directed drive between states was lower across subcortical connections. This pattern suggests altered network dynamics rather than altered network architecture in MS. Findings from this study characterize the functional network dynamics of neurodegeneration in MS, which may inform future development of network-based approaches for monitoring disease progression.

item.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
item.description:
[预印本] medRxiv
Exposure to armed conflict can leave persistent effects on mental health, yet its neurophysiological correlates remain poorly characterized, particularly in populations exposed to prolonged violence outside narrowly defined post traumatic stress disorder samples. Here we examined resting state electroencephalographic activity in 122 Colombian adults, including 74 participants exposed to armed conflict and 48 controls. Eyes closed EEG was analysed for 240 seconds per participant. We quantified absolute and relative spectral power across delta, theta, alpha and beta bands and regional functional connectivity using weighted phase lag index in theta, alpha and beta. Group comparisons were adjusted for age, education, sex and assessment year, with correction across 78 EEG contrasts. Median occipital and global alpha power was lower in exposed participants, although adjusted estimates were close to the null and confidence intervals were broad. Temporal theta relative power was lower in exposed participants at nominal significance, but this association did not survive Holm correction. No spectral power or regional connectivity contrast remained significant after multiple testing correction. Exploratory associations between EEG measures and MoCA performance were modest in participants with confirmed scores. These findings provide a systematic characterization of resting EEG after exposure to armed conflict in a population shaped by prolonged violence and displacement. They also indicate that large or widespread alterations in resting spectral power and connectivity were not detectable with the current sample and analytical framework, while defining candidate signals and methodological priorities for larger studies of conflict related brain health.

item.title: An amygdala-mediated simulation-to-decision cascade aligns interbrain dynamics to solve social dilemmas.
item.description:
Nature neuroscience
Mutual cooperation (MC) requires independent decision-makers to coordinate under uncertainty about each other's intentions. Using simultaneous intracranial electroencephalography from epilepsy-patient dyads playing a real-time iterated prisoner's dilemma, we identified neurocognitive mechanisms that enable interacting brains to align during mutual cooperation. Amygdala interbrain representational alignment (IBRA), similarity in fine-grained neural spectral patterns across partners, emerged selectively during MC and predicted trial-by-trial outcomes. Early θ-suppression-characterized IBRA reflected rapid, history-sensitive alignment, whereas later IBRA, characterized by low-frequency suppression and γ increases, supported coordinated commitment and action. Furthermore, mutual cooperation relied on an amygdala-mediated, simulation-to-decision cascade, operationalized here as a model-based prospective estimate of partner cooperation that guided self-choice. Amygdala low-frequency suppression tracked this prospective estimate of partner cooperation and θ-γ coupling linked this partner estimate to self-decision processes. Conditional cooperators strategically relied on partner tracking, whereas unconditional cooperators leveraged dispositional tolerance of uncertainty to transition into anticipatory neural alignment. These findings reveal the neural interdependency underpinning MC, redefining cooperation not as isolated decision-making but as a dynamic, interbrain, cognitive alignment.

item.title: EEG Resting-State Beta Band Dynamic Functional Connectivity Reveals State-Dependent Disruption of Language Network Lateralisation in First-Episode Schizophrenia.
item.description:
Neuropsychologia
Language disorganisation is a core feature of schizophrenia with significant functional consequences. However, its neurophysiological substrates remain poorly characterised, particularly in the early stages of the illness. This study investigated whether first-episode schizophrenia (FES) is associated with disruption in the organisation of language-network lateralisation, using both static and dynamic functional connectivity metrics in the EEG beta band. Thirty-one FES patients and 32 age-matched healthy volunteer subjects (HVS) underwent resting-state 64-channel EEG. Source-level connectivity was estimated using the weighted phase lag index with sliding windows, yielding 979 connectivity matrices per participant. Brain network states (BNS) were identified via k-means clustering. Static connectivity was obtained by time-averaging. Temporal features, graph-theoretical metrics, and language-network laterality indices were extracted for both whole-network and language-specific analyses. Group comparisons used permutation-based tests with family-wise error correction. Static connectivity yielded no significant group differences in any metric. Dynamic analysis identified six BNS. FES showed a significant increase in the variability of the temporal dynamics and graph-theory features of BNS5, a state characterised by parieto-occipital dominance. The core language network laterality index was significantly reduced in FES within BNS1, a state characterised by auditory-visual dominance. BNS1 occurrence correlated negatively with language disorganisation scores. Dynamic BNS-specific language network metrics correlated with verbal fluency performance exclusively in FES. These findings demonstrate that language dysfunction in early psychosis is expressed as state-dependent disruption of brain network stability and language lateralisation, detectable only through dynamic connectivity analysis.

item.title: Cortical Cholinergic Pathway Degeneration Reflects Cognitive Impairment and Dementia in Parkinson's Disease.
item.description:
Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
Background Cognitive impairment is a prevalent and debilitating feature of Parkinson's disease (PD). Increasing evidence from postmortem and in vivo positron emission tomography imaging studies supports cholinergic dysfunction in PD. There is, however, little evidence regarding the influence of the structural integrity of cortical cholinergic pathways that emanate from the nucleus basalis of Meynert (NBM). Objectives To investigate the association between cognition and the structural integrity of medial and lateral cortical cholinergic projection pathways in PD. Methods Neuropsychological assessment, T1 imaging, and high angular resolution diffusion imaging (HARDI) were acquired from 108 participants with PD (41 female, mean age 71.3 years) and 41 control participants (22 female, mean age 70.6 years). Streamlines representing three cortical cholinergic pathways (one medial and two lateral) from the NBM were extracted from anatomically constrained tractography. Structural integrity was compared across controls and cognitive subgroups (PD with normal cognition [PD-N], with mild cognitive impairment [PD-MCI], and with dementia [PDD]) and using a continuous global measure of cognition. Results In PD, we found evidence that lower cognitive performance was associated with increased mean diffusivity across all pathways, especially the perisylvian component of the lateral pathway. In those individuals with dementia, increased free water fraction and decreased fractional anisotropy and fiber density and cross-section was detected across all pathways. Conclusions Degeneration of the cortical cholinergic system is associated with cognitive decline in PD. Future work should determine whether pathway degeneration predicts future cognitive decline and dementia. © 2026 The Author(s).
